Ava (People Ops): FYI - coordinating a short sabbatical question for Maya. She plans to be in Bali ~10 weeks, doing ~10 hrs/week of paid consulting for a US client while remaining on Redwood payroll. Question: does WFH stipend continue and are there tax/employer obligations?
Maya Patel: correct — 10 weeks (late May -> early Aug). Still on Redwood payroll, not changing home base. Client pays me personally via Stripe. WFH stipend would cover coworking + internet.
Marco (Payroll): quick Qs: 1) exact dates, 2) payroll bank/account unchanged?, 3) home base declared as OR (Oregon)? Also note outside income paid to employee can change withholding/reporting depending on country.
Maya Patel: dates 2026-05-22 -> 2026-08-01. Payroll same US bank. Home base remains OR.
Priya (Legal): high-level: Indonesia has a ~183-day residency rule but there are other triggers (source of income, local regs). Short stays under 90 days often avoid residency but don't guarantee no local obligations — e.g., local biz-license or withholding rules may apply sooner. If payroll/employer risk is non-trivial we'll need local counsel. Not formal advice.
Jon (Benefits): stipend policy: continues for temporary remote work that doesn't change home base. We ask for notification >30 days; extended travel reviews apply. Since she remains employed and will not change home base, stipend should remain but needs manager approval. If sabbatical were unpaid we'd treat differently.
Devon (Manager): I approve the time pattern and stipend continuation pending payroll/legal checks. Will keep regular check-ins.
Marco (Payroll): action items: 1) run Indonesia country risk check for employer reporting/filing, 2) confirm pay method doesn't trigger additional banking compliance, 3) flag that Stripe client retainer is outside personal income for tax purposes and Maya should consult tax advisor. I'll post the country risk note by EOD tomorrow.
Priya (Legal): agree. If shes contracting for a US client while physically in ID, advise she avoid signing local contracts as a Redwood representative and not invoice under Redwood. I'll loop in APAC counsel for a quick read (1-2 business days).
Ava (People Ops): to keep this lightweight: Maya, please submit the short-term remote form with travel dates and home-base confirmation and get manager sign-off. Payroll/Legal  please post concrete flags within 48 hours. We'll pause any stipend changes until confirmation.
PeopleOpsBot: Reminder - submit short-term remote form: https://redwood-internal/self-serve/remote-form (fields: dates, location, contact, intended work).
Maya Patel: submitted the form and attached client retainer details (paid to me personally).
Marco (Payroll): received the form, running the Indonesia check. Note: local authorities can sometimes request registration/withholding even for short engagements if they view source-of-income rules as triggered; probability low but non-zero.
Priya (Legal): looping APAC counsel now. If counsel flags medium-or-higher risk, options: stagger travel, limit client work while abroad, or implement temporary withholding/reporting.
Ava (People Ops): summary of next steps: 1) Payroll - country risk report (EOD tomorrow), 2) Legal - counsel read (48h), 3) Manager - confirm stipend approval in form, 4) Maya - avoid invoicing as "Redwood" or using company resources while abroad. Reconvene when reports in. Thanks. :pray:
Devon (Manager): approved stipend on the form.
Maya Patel: thanks all - I'll pause any client invoicing until final.
PeopleOpsBot: Thread archived after inactivity.
